title: Article 351 — Directive for development of the Hindi language

content.overview: Article 351 directs that it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language, to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India, and to secure its enrichment by assimilating the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and in the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule, and by drawing, wherever necessary or desirable, for its vocabulary, primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
content.glance: Union duty: promote and develop Hindi as a medium for India’s composite culture; enrich from Hindustani and Eighth Schedule languages; vocabulary primarily from Sanskrit, secondarily from other languages.
content.study:
Article 351 is a Directive (not a justiciable Fundamental Right) for development of Hindi:
1. Promote the spread of Hindi.
2. Develop it as a medium of expression for all elements of India’s composite culture.
3. Enrich by assimilating forms, style and expressions from Hindustani and Eighth Schedule languages.
4. Vocabulary: primarily Sanskrit, secondarily other languages.

Examination: Union duty; composite culture; Eighth Schedule; Sanskrit primary for vocabulary.

sections.heading: Key directive
sections.body: Union shall promote spread of Hindi; develop it for composite culture; enrich from Hindustani and Eighth Schedule languages; vocabulary primarily from Sanskrit, secondarily from other languages.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What does Article 351 direct regarding Hindi?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Article 351 provides that it shall be the duty of the Union to promote the spread of the Hindi language, to develop it so that it may serve as a medium of expression for all the elements of the composite culture of India, and to secure its enrichment by assimilating without interfering with its genius the forms, style and expressions used in Hindustani and in the other languages of India specified in the Eighth Schedule, and by drawing, wherever necessary or desirable, for its vocabulary, primarily on Sanskrit and secondarily on other languages.
